findings.title: Keep the requester's team/org scope on approved runs; L-401 pins tenant only
findings.current_state: The L-401 fix makes executeApproval() pass a bare `new CapabilityScope(tenantId: <row tenant>)`, and ResolveTenantFromCaller returns that option without calling the ScopeResolver. teamId, organizationId, attributes and any resolver-attached query factory are all dropped. Before the fix they came from the resolver. Reproduced on the audit tree with the IdempotencyHelpers harness and the default resolver: a user with current_tenant_id=t1, current_team_id=team-9 and current_organization_id=org-3 gets run() ctx [t1, team-9, org-3] on a direct invoke, but [t1, null, null] when the same invoke is approved and accepted. The approval row cannot restore them because buildApprovalRequired stamps only tenant_id, and ApprovalManager copies that string into the `scope` (scope_json) column.
findings.recommended_state: An approved run and the original-actor re-check see the scope the request was stamped with: tenant, team and organization (plus JSON-safe attributes), not a tenant-only scope.
findings.rationale: A spec rule (D-006 step 5, spec.md:1818) says an approved request runs 'under the original caller + scope + idempotency key'. The package's DefaultScopeResolver and the spec's AppScopeResolver example (spec.md:1619-1622) both fill teamId, and CapabilityContext exposes teamId()/organizationId() for capabilities to use. So a capability that re-resolves resources by team, or a host ScopedQueryFactory that narrows by $scope->teamId, sees null team on exactly the path where a human signed off. That is inconsistent at best. At worst a `when($scope->teamId, ...)` factory drops the team constraint and resolves resources across the whole tenant. The audit row for the approved run also records team_id=null (AuditLogger:53), and authorize() is re-checked under a different scope shape than the original request had. Pinning the tenant (L-401) was right. Pinning only the tenant is the regression.
findings.implementation_hint: (1) In InvokePipeline::buildApprovalRequired, stamp `'scope' => ['tenant_id' => $ctx->tenantId(), 'team_id' => $ctx->teamId(), 'organization_id' => $ctx->organizationId()]` (add attributes only if the owner wants them persisted). The scope_json column and both stores already carry `scope`. (2) Add a small `CapabilityScope::fromRow(array $row)` that reads that array, and falls back to `tenant_id` only when the stored scope is a legacy string or null. Use it in CapabilityRegistry::executeApproval (keep the null-tenant rows resolving as today) and in OriginalActorAuthorizer. (3) Unit test: extend ApproverTenantResolutionTest so a requester with current_team_id/current_organization_id sees the same teamId()/organizationId() in run() on accept and resume as on a direct invoke, including after switching tenant (team from the row, not the new tenant).

notes: Iteration 6, core scope only (packages/laravel-capabilities), tree a85ec63. The only core src changes since iteration 5 are 8565cf4 (L-401) and be02cb7 (L-402). I traced approval/tenant/scope and idempotency end to end: row stamping (InvokePipeline::buildApprovalRequired), approver placement (ApprovalManager::approverTenant -> ResolveTenantFromCaller::tenantOfPrincipal), the resume tenant guard (ApprovalResumer), the original-actor re-check (OriginalActorAuthorizer), execution (CapabilityRegistry::executeApproval -> resolve_scope early return on the `scope` option), idempotency lookup/claim/settle (IdempotencyGuard, InvokeResultFinalizer, both stores' expired-row claim swap), and the provider wiring. L-401 verification: correct for the tenant. run(), authorize re-check, audit and the key row all land in the row tenant, and the pending_approval key row settles (the guard keys on ctx tenantId, matching the stamp). It regressed the team/org dimensions (L-501, reproduced with a throwaway script in the session scratchpad against the audit tree's bootstrap and IdempotencyHelpers; the audit tree was not modified). L-402 verification: correct and complete. Every Throwable from the resolver in tenantOfPrincipal yields null (fail-closed forbidden), unwraps the RuntimeException wrapper for reporting, and counts approver_scope_failed_total{caller}. Accept, reject and the user-resume guard all go through it. Considered and not raised: a pre-lookup failure on an approved re-run (for example stored input that no longer passes schema after a deploy) leaves the key row at pending_approval until its TTL (rare, TTL-bounded, and a revalidator hook exists); a host setting approval.ttl_hours above idempotency.ttl_hours lets a retry after key expiry open a second approval (a config choice, and spec says reuse after expiry is a new key; defaults are equal at 24h); an approved execution for a requester who has since left the row's tenant runs in that tenant, relying on authorize() (the resolver contract has no membership probe, and failing closed would re-break the legitimate tenant-switcher case L-401 fixed). Deferred items were honoured.
